full_judgment: 13. Now, So far the question regarding whether the claims of the respondents are disputed question of facts, it appears that the officer of the forest department before making inspection of the timbers issued notice to the respondents asking them to be present at the time of inspection. Accordingly the inspection of the timbers was conducted and found it measuring weighing to about 1610 cubic feet in place of 1750 cubic feet as claimed by respondent No.1 Azizul Hoque Badsha who by filing an application stated that he has stored total 1750 cubic feet in Ali Kadam Depot No.92. It also appears that upon inspection of the timbers stored by respondent No.2 Badol Kanti Sharma it was found as 9480 cubic feet in place of 11000 cubic feet. It further appears that after completion of the inspection the aforesaid timbers were given under the custody of the respondents. So, now the appellants cannot take a plea that the respondents raised disputed question of fact. It also appears that before passing the impugned judgment the concerned authorities were previously directed by the High Court Division in other two writ petitions mentioned above to deliver the same kind of goods to those petitioners but they did not take any legal step against those judgments. So the presumption is that they have delivered the goods as per the judgments of those two writ petitions. So in the facts and circumstances as stated above we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General for the appellants and consequently the appeal is liable to be dis-missed.
